rationale: After five commands from the Decalogue, Matthew's list ends "and love your neighbor as yourself" (19:19, BSB). Leviticus 19:18 reads "Do not seek revenge or bear a grudge against any of your people, but love your neighbor as yourself. I am the LORD" (BSB): the BSB has the same five words. The Greek matches the Septuagint too: Matthew 19:19 reads agapēseis ton plēsion sou hōs seauton in every edition on Bible Hub, and Swete's Septuagint of Leviticus 19:18 has the same words. The command is not one of the Ten, but Jesus gives it as one of "the commandments" in answer to "Which ones?" (19:17-18), so the type is quotation and the label explicit, the same introducing marker as the Decalogue row (conn-matt19-commandments-exodus20). Matthew alone adds it: Mark 10:19 and Luke 18:20 do not have it. The NABRE note on 19:18-19 says Matthew "adds Lv 19:18" and that the combination is "partially the same as Paul's enumeration" in Romans 13:9. Calvin reads the added line as "general explanation" of the others. The verse is quoted again at Matthew 22:39 and at Matthew 5:43 in a shorter form ("Love your neighbor"); those verses are left to their own lessons.
